• Proteinuria, deﬁned as 300 mg/24 h (gold standard) or 1þ on reagent strip, is a diagnostic criterion for PE in some country
guidelines (Scott et al., 2020), but is not an absolute requirement for the diagnosis of PE (Magee et al., 2014; ACOG, 2013;
Tranquilli et al., 2014), because pathophysiological features of PE can be present before the kidney involvement is severe
enough to induce proteinuria (Chaiworapongsa et al., 2014), and because proteinuria might not be present in complications
such as eclampsia, acute renal failure or pulmonary edema (Thornton et al., 2010).

• Other maternal organ involvement: Central nervous system (severe headache and/or hyperreﬂexia with clonus, altered mental
status), liver (double or more liver transaminases), kidney [creatinine >90 mmol/L, or double of previous creatinine, or oliguria
(<500 mL/d)], hematological complications [thrombocytopenia (platelet count <150,000/mL)] (Poon et al., 2019), or new
onset of visual impairment with retinopathy, retinal detachment, or cortical blindness (Abu Samra, 2013).
• Utero-placental involvement: Fetal growth restriction, stillbirth or abnormal umbilical artery Doppler wave (Poon et al., 2019).
